title: Quick changes can leave an older state in the data file
goal: What is on disk after the last change is the last state, whatever the disk does.

acceptance_criteria.text: Once flush() has resolved, the data file holds the latest state of the store, however long each write takes (reported: two changes close together, and the file kept the first).
Writes never overlap: a write starts only after the one before it has finished. Changes made while a write is in flight are saved by one write after it, not by one write per change.

A write that fails is reported through onError, once, and does not keep later changes from being saved. It is not tried again: the next write is the one the next change causes. flush() resolves all the same; it never rejects.
persist() keeps its interface: the write and onError options, flush() and stop(). Changes made after stop() are not saved. A test fails without the fix.

context.notes: The write option exists so that a test can decide how long a write takes and whether it fails. Keep node:http and node:fs only; no dependencies.
